items.title: Cancellation-Free Constrained SquareCB for Safe Controller Selection
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study constrained contextual bandits, in which a learner chooses one of $K$ actions in each round to minimize loss while keeping the expected cost of its play below a budget. items.title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. items.title: Done, But Still Working: Anytime Evaluation of When Coding Agents Should Stop
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents often continue working after their own tests pass. Does this additional work improve the patch, and how much could be saved by stopping earlier? items.title: MM-ReportBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Report Generation from Tables
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ability to generate multimodal reports integrating fluent narratives with faithful visualizations from tabular data, has become a cornerstone capability for modern vision-language models in practical domains such as finance, healthcare, and policy making. items.title: Learning Regions of Attraction for Transverse Feedback Linearization under Controller Singularities
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transverse feedback linearization (TFL) achieves path following by exactly linearizing the error dynamics, but its controller is undefined on a singular set, such as zero speed for a unicycle or zero thrust for a quadrotor. items.title: CrossEnv: Synthesizing Verifiable Cross-Environment Tasks for Long-Horizon Agent Training
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Executable synthetic environments provide scalable training tasks and verifiable feedback for long-horizon agents. items.title: ForecastGym: A Live, Controlled, and Replayable Benchmark for Forecasting Agents
items.summary: arXiv:2611.23045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents built on large language models (LLMs) increasingly forecast real-world events by searching the Web and reasoning over what they find. items.title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
items.summary: arXiv:2611.23074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable. items.title: Perception into Imagination: Executable Memory for World Models

items.summary: arXiv:2611.21644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel in vision-language tasks; yet, whether they maintain consistent understanding of information-rich visuals (InfoVis) when the surface language changes remains unclear. items.summary: arXiv:2611.21650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sycophancy in large language models is often measured as agreement with the user, yet agreement can be appropriate when the user's claim is valid, their preference is genuine, or their experience warrants acknowledgment. items.title: Inventa: Decentralized Self-Improving Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can generate research ideas and improve scientific discovery through iterative experimentation. The structure of this mindset is this: the coming of a future doomsday is believed to sweep away everything, which then makes everything else seem not very important compared with it. This belief itself changes the weight given to things. I want to make two points. First, I want to explicitly rebut a claim some people make: that we need to stop before things end.[2][4]My rebuttal is: anything is easiest to stop before it has started…

items.title: Structure Constants of Planar N=4 SYM at Any Coupling
items.summary: We recast a recent conjecture for structure constants in planar N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory in a separation-of-variables-inspired form suitable for non-perturbative analysis. All state-dependent information enters through the quantum spectral curve. As a showcase, we compute at finite coupling the three-point functions of two half-BPS operators and the spin-two member of the Konishi multiplet. Our results span weak to strong coupling, reproduce the known perturbative and string-theory limits, and are consistent with conformal-bootstrap bounds. We also obtain new six- and seven-loop perturbative coefficients and extract new strong-coupling data from high-precision numerical fits.

items.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
items.summary: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. Given access to the full research transcript and the ability to run experiments, human auditors mostly fail to distinguish sabotaged from benign research: they achieve an AUROC of 0.59, not significantly better than chance, and fully identify the specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. items.title: Controllable Chains of Thought Can Reveal Less, Even Without Evasion Training
items.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. Averaged across evaluations and CoT lengths, weighted by side-task-success counts, the CoT monitorability metric g-mean$^2$ falls from 0.94 for the base model to 0.68 for the model…

items.title: Margin Dynamics for Large Language Model Alignment
items.summary: Practitioners choose among LLM alignment methods largely by trial and error. We provide a theoretical foundation: each pairwise method defines a vector field on the probability simplex that governs how the model redistributes mass between preferred and dispreferred completions. Projecting onto a single preferred/dispreferred pair reduces this to a one-dimensional margin ODE with a closed-form solution. These solutions reveal that DPO margins grow without bound (logarithmically as $O(\log t)$ in the gradient-flow limit) while IPO margins converge to a finite $1/(2τ)$; that label noise induces a qualitative phase transition in DPO (unbounded $\to$ bounded) but affects IPO only quantitatively; and that gradient concentration under asymmetric weighting governs trainability at scale. We confirm all three predictions across five model…

items.title: ONAM: Fitting Orthogonal Neural Additive Models for Post-Hoc Interpretability of Black-Box Predictions
items.summary: Modern machine learning models, such as artificial neural networks, achieve high predictive performance through increasingly complex black-box architectures, limiting their use in settings where transparency, interpretability, and fairness are required. Here we present the R package ONAM, which provides a novel and practical implementation of functional decomposition, a technique to facilitate the interpretability of black-box models through structured effect representations. ONAM implements an algorithmic framework for the post-hoc decomposition of predictions into components associated with different input features. The package is designed for usability and efficiency, including functionalities for visualization as well as quantitative measures to assess interpretability. As a model-agnostic method, it can be applied to a wide range…

items.title: Optimistic Verifiers Get Hacked: Reward Hacking Under an Exact Process Oracle
items.summary: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards inherits whatever its verifier gets wrong. Outside mathematics and code the verifier is a proxy, a rubric, a learned judge or a hand-written checker, and its distance from the true objective is never measured, so a rising reward cannot be told apart from a hack. We build a setting where the true reward is exactly computable at the process level: executable authorization policies over 124,416 contexts admit an oracle that lists every minimal sufficient reason for every decision. We compile these policies into exact process rewards, degrade the verifier along seven realistic axes (outcome-only, sufficiency, recall-only, extraction noise, coarse taxonomy, stale policy, LLM judge), and train against each while the exact verifier scores every rollout. Four phenotypes appear. Optimistic verifiers…

items.title: On Friends at Frontier Labs
items.summary: I am deeply uncertain about whether or not it is a good idea to get my friends to quit working at frontier AI labs. I am against people working at frontier AI labs in general, but perhaps downstream of this, all my friends in the labs have sophisticated justifications for their being there that seem plausibly true to me. More broadly, if this was not a painfully difficult question, the community wouldn't have split over it, and there are enough rationalists and EAs in the labs that it seems obvious to me that the community has split. items.title: Emergent Steering Beyond Endpoint Alignment in Chemical Reaction Models
items.summary: Machine learning models for chemical reaction prediction are usually evaluated by endpoint accuracy, but endpoint correctness alone does not reveal how a model represents chemical transformation or why it fails. We introduce UniRxnAxis, a unified forward-retrosynthesis framework that models both tasks as direction-conditioned endpoint redistribution in a shared latent space. This shared latent geometry allows the learned displacement (from the encoder source state $S_0$ to the decoder-facing transformed state $S_1$) to be decomposed into an endpoint-parallel component and an endpoint-orthogonal residual, which we call emergent steering. Our evaluation shows that emergent steering is functionally…

items.title: Cryonics as Cause Area
items.summary: TLDR: Cryonics should be considered as part of a diversified portfolio of altruistic projects. I estimate, using ~3% chance of revival and a modest post-revival lifespan (~20,000 years), that current biopreservation is roughly on par with top GiveWell charities in terms of QALYs per dollar. Scaled up, it could plausibly be dozens of times better. There are various complications, of course, but it still seems reasonable that cryonics complements rather than competes with things like AI-safety work. items.title: Manifold and Polymarket are biased against "nothing ever happens"
items.summary: While investigating whether prediction markets are calibrated, I found a prediction market bias towards "something happens". The official plot here looks like Manifold consistently slightly overprices "YES", but as I show, the bias depends on the type of question: * YES needs something to happen. items.title: Conflict-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Aligned Action Spaces for Cross-Game Generalization
items.summary: Zero-shot cross-game generalization aims to consolidate accessible source-game experts into a single vision-language model (VLM) that controls unseen games from raw pixels without target-game parameter updates. While multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) mitigates offline exposure bias and single-game reinforcement learning (RL) overfitting, scaling it to autoregressive VLMs faces two bottlenecks. First, token-to-action misalignment from subword length bias distorts discrete action probabilities and uncertainty margins. Second, multi-teacher policy conflict arises as source teachers under incompatible dynamics issue contradictory closed-loop corrections, causing negative transfer. We propose CAMOPD (Conflict-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation), a post-training framework that resolves multi-teacher policy conflict within an…

items.title: The Exact Optimal Delivery Scheme for the Cyclically $L$-Separated Placement in Multi-Access Coded Caching
items.summary: This paper investigates the $(K, L, M, N)$ multi-access coded caching (MACC) system introduced by Hachem et al. The system consists of a server storing $N$ equal-sized files, $K$ cache nodes, each with a storage capacity of $M$ files, and $K$ users, each accessing $L$ consecutive cache nodes in a cyclic wrap-around topology. The server transmits coded information to the users via an error-free capacitated broadcast channel, such that each user obtains its own requested file as a combination of the server transmission and the accessible caches' content. Our objective is to minimize the worst-case transmission load over all possible user demands. First, for the cyclically $L$-separated placement, we derive a new converse bound using the acyclic index coding bound. By carefully counting all valid cache supports, the proposed converse…

items.title: The Siren Song of the Inside Game
items.summary: BLUF: There’s a structural pull to overinvest in cosying up with frontier labs relative to publicly holding them to account. Now seems like a good time to rebalance. When thinking about influencing an organisation (like, say, a frontier lab), it’s useful to distinguish between the inside game and the outside game. The inside game means trying to work with the insiders: building trust and influence with them, and looking for compromises. The outside game means applying external pressure: building broad political will and being willing to take a more adversarial posture. In an ideal world, you do a mixture of the two: the good cop and the bad cop, the carrot and the stick, and so on. But AI safety does not have some single strategy. items.summary: Existing information sources rely upon authorities to decide which information flows to their readers, authorities whom readers cannot readily see, and whose decisions they cannot readily contest. I seek to address this problem with the following protocol: Verisphere – a permissionless, on-chain claim graph in which claims (nodes) and evidence links (edges) carry stake, scored and settled daily by public rules, without any refereeing authority. items.title: Same Question, Different Lies:\texorpdfstring{\\}{ } Cross-Context Consistency (C\textsuperscript{3}) for Black-Box Sandbagging Detection
items.summary: As language models grow more capable, accurate capability evaluation becomes essential for safety decisions. If models can deliberately underperform on dangerous capability evaluations---a behavior known as \emph{sandbagging}---they may evade safety measures designed for their true capability level. We introduce Cross-Context Consistency (C³), a general framework for unsupervised black-box sandbagging detection that exploits a fundamental asymmetry: when a model truly lacks capability, its confusion manifests consistently across paraphrased questions, but when a capable model feigns incompetence, its strategic choices about \emph{how} to appear weak create detectable inconsistencies. Our framework is agnostic to the specific consistency metric and aggregation method; we present a simple instantiation using embedding cosine distance and…

items.title: Stress-Testing the Truth Advantage in Language Model Debates
items.summary: As AI systems become more capable, evaluation becomes difficult when the evaluator cannot independently verify the model's answer. This is the scalable oversight problem. AI debate addresses it by placing two language models in opposition before a weaker judge, testing whether the truthful side has a systematic advantage over the deceptive side, a property referred to as the Truth Advantage. In this setting the judge is the verifier, and the strength of the protocol rests entirely on how reliable that verifier is. Prior empirical work supports the Truth Advantage under standard benchmark conditions, leaving open whether it holds when question wording or structure changes while the correct answer remains fixed. We establish consultancy and debate baselines on the QuALITY reading-comprehension benchmark using two independent judge models…

items.title: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale
items.summary: Aligning autonomous agents with human intent remains a central challenge in modern AI. A key manifestation of this challenge is reward hacking, whereby agents appear successful under the evaluation signal while violating the intended objective. Reward hacking has been observed across a wide range of settings, yet methods for reliably measuring it at scale remain lacking. In this work, we introduce a new evaluation paradigm for measuring reward hacking. Whereas prior studies have primarily analyzed it post hoc by inspecting agent trajectories, we instead embed detectable reward hacking opportunities directly into environments. This makes their exploitation verifiable by design, enabling deterministic and automated measurement of whether and how agents exploit such vulnerabilities. We instantiate this approach in TextArena and release…

items.title: Control OSWorld: An AI Control Environment for GUI Computer Use Agents
items.summary: AI agents that operate a computer through its graphical user interface (GUI) are being widely deployed. AI control studies how to prevent an AI system from causing harm even if it is misaligned and actively trying to do so. Most control research to date has focused on coding agents, leaving computer use largely unexplored. We introduce Control OSWorld, a control evaluation that pairs 318 tasks from OSWorld with 81 harmful side tasks (e.g., exfiltrating a private file) that an agent must complete without being caught. We use Control OSWorld to create and study control monitors that detect malicious agents interacting with a GUI. We find that a weaker monitor can reliably distinguish honest from malicious trajectories produced by a more capable agent when it sees the full trajectory (97% recall at 3% false positive rate). However, when…

items.title: Probing Misalignment in LLMs with Adaptive Environment-Level Red-Teaming
items.summary: Frontier language models deployed as autonomous agents can scheme, sandbag, and game evaluations when structural incentives are present. Methods for surfacing these behaviors fall into two categories: prompt-level red-teaming adapts to the target but never changes the environment, while environment-level audits and benchmarks build realistic settings with tools and incentives, but never adapt to the target, reporting aggregate rates instead. Neither approach identifies the environmental conditions that elicit misalignment in a given model. We propose adaptive environment-level red-teaming, a three-phase methodology that iterates on the environment rather than the prompt: it fingerprints target behavior across six dimensions, generates a baseline scenario within a realistic professional context, then iteratively modifies environmental…

items.title: Open Problems in LLM Self-Prediction
items.summary: We tested how well LLMs can predict what they will do in long-horizon agentic environments. We found LLMs are poorly calibrated and overconfident about how well they will perform; stronger models rise to their own inflated expectations, which makes them merely appear to be better self-forecasters. We release a detailed evaluation suite ([code and data link redacted for double-blind review; see supplementary]), so that self-predictive ability can be tracked in future models: a sudden step in self-knowledge above our baseline could be a warning sign for long-horizon scheming, since self-knowledge plausibly is a prerequisite for it. items.title: Reward Hacking as a Transmissible Strategy in Multi-Agent Coding Systems
items.summary: Multi-agent systems are increasingly used to solve coding tasks by coordinating agents that share code and plans. These agents are often optimized with reinforcement learning (RL) using automated evaluators, but bypassing evaluation can earn reward without producing a genuine solution. Prior work has largely treated reward hacking as a single-agent failure. In this work, we show that a reward-hacking strategy elicited in one agent can propagate to others and affect system coordination. Across four open-weight backbones, coding RL elicits and amplifies reward hacking in two settings: explicit mechanism descriptions in the system prompt and mid-training that models upstream exposure to facts about the coding environment. Using post-RL agents from the mid-training setting as sources, we observe propagation through code and shared memory…

items.title: When Vulnerability Is Not Exploitation: Reward Hacking in Coding Agents
items.summary: Reward hacking is often treated as a single failure mode in which an agent exploits imperfections in an evaluation mechanism rather than completing the intended task. In agentic coding environments, however, environment vulnerability and agent behavior are distinct: the same structural weakness may coexist with honest task completion, effort-substituting shortcuts, or deliberate exploitation. We study this distinction at both the environment and trajectory levels. We analyze 3,009 environment-review findings to develop an intervention-based taxonomy of structural vulnerabilities, and 5,343 trajectories from six model variants across anonymized machine-learning engineering environments to distinguish honest behavior, shortcut behavior, and executed reward hacking. We find that structural vulnerability does not directly translate into…

items.title: Sensitive but Not Specific: What a Trusted Policy's Logs Can and Cannot Say About Reward Hacking
items.summary: When an agent is updated, operators may want to screen the candidate before running it, using only trajectories logged by the trusted incumbent. Off-policy evaluation (OPE) is a natural offline verification tool, but importance-sampling estimates become unreliable precisely when a candidate departs strongly from logged behaviour. We ask whether this failure is itself informative: can log-side support diagnostics distinguish reward hacking from benign change? In a controlled Wordle agent testbed with exact action probabilities, we construct and gate-certify faithful, benign-drift, benign-improving, degraded, and reward-hacked policies—the hackers distilled from scripted proxy-farming teachers after hacking failed to emerge across seven escalating GRPO runs. items.title: Oversight Under Flooding: An Unidentifiable Attack and a Robust Defense
items.summary: An adversary need not fool a verifier. Instead, it can change the conditions under which the verifier operates. Deployed agent architectures terminate in a human approving consequential actions, and that human is modelled throughout the literature as an oracle: fixed accuracy, unbounded throughput. We treat the approver as a capacity-constrained component and ask what an adversary achieves by injecting benign filler–perturbing no individual decision, changing only volume. Our central result is a comparative static: the sign of an optimising defender’s threshold adjustment under flooding is governed by $\eta'$, the derivative of the elasticity of reviewer reliability with respect to load, and the slope of the reliability curve does not appear, though it is the quantity practitioners reason about. items.title: Fooling One Fools Them All: Universal Over-Optimization in Model-Graded RL
items.summary: Reinforcement learning has been crucial for helping improve models in domains with cheap verifiable rewards such as coding. However, many useful tasks, such as alignment research and conceptual thinking, lack such rewards. Moreover, reliable human feedback is expensive to collect for such tasks. Model graders therefore offer a scalable alternative, and can serve as both a reward signal during training and as a proxy for tracking task progress. However, policies can learn to over-optimize against these graders during training, so stronger held-out graders are often used to track progress more reliably. Our work questions this assumed reliability, demonstrating the existence of universal over-optimization, where scores from training and held-out graders, across model families and scales, increase without a corresponding improvement in…

items.title: Can People Distinguish Human and AI Agency in Humanoid Teleoperation? A Preliminary Study of Agency Perception
items.summary: Can people distinguish between human and AI agency in humanoid teleoperation? We conducted a preliminary online study ($N=50$) in which participants viewed short interaction clips generated by either a Human Operator or an AI Control and judged the perceived source of control. Results suggest that participants often struggled to distinguish between the two conditions in brief interactions. Qualitative responses indicate that judgments were primarily influenced by perceived naturalness, temporal coordination, and consistency across speech, facial expression, and gesture. items.title: A Second Order Transport Scheme for Dynamic Portfolio Subspaces under a Varying Risk Metric
items.summary: We analyze the transport of portfolio exposures between moving subspaces under a varying positive definite risk metric. The reference evolution is the induced connection obtained from the ambient connection of minimum norm in fixed asset coordinates. Geometric mean alignment and a symmetric Procrustes construction cancel the term and yield reversible updates with second order global accuracy. items.title: Unconditionally Positive Nonstandard Finite Difference Schemes for $p$-Laplacian Reaction--Diffusion Equations
items.summary: We propose a conservative, semi-implicit nonstandard finite difference scheme for the reaction--diffusion equation $u_t=λ(|u_x|^{p-2}u_x)_x+f(u)$, $p>1$, where, as is customary, the $p$-Laplacian is regularized by a parameter $\eps>0$. The scheme combines a denominator function, a lagged diffusion coefficient, and a nonlocal treatment of the loss part of the reaction. For every time step and mesh size we prove that the scheme is well posed and positive, that it preserves an invariant region $[0,K]$ whenever the reaction admits one, and that it reproduces every constant equilibrium exactly. Without reaction, it conserves mass, satisfies a discrete maximum principle, and, for $1 2$. The truncation error is $O(k+h^2)$ at interior nodes. items.title: Tight PAC-Bayes Generalisation Guarantees for Large Language Model Judges
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) judges are increasingly used to monitor the outputs of LLM-based AI agents, yet formal guarantees on the reliability of these judges remain largely absent, limiting confidence in their use for safety-critical oversight. We consider certifying such a judge and define its risk over safety classifications of prompt--response pairs drawn from a deployed generator. We apply a PAC-Bayes framework to this setting, refining existing compression-based methodology with the use of tighter bounds and more efficient coding. We show that standard parameter-efficient fine-tuning can yield non-vacuous and even tight certificates for safety judges, for both classification and Brier risk, without holding out data for validation. We introduce LoRA-GT, which shares a single quantisation scale across layers and achieves the…

items.title: Whose Effect Is It? How Objectives Inflate Learned Subspace Interventions
items.summary: TL;DR: Mech interp literature rewards learned parts that are bigger than the whole, while searching for the best location to do activation patching. We proved mathematically and tested why a part can have a larger effect, and what the problem with it is. In short, the extra mostly comes from the objective, not the model. items.title: WETW: Learning Pair-Specific Weighted Euclidean Distances for Efficient DTW Search
items.summary: arXiv:2611.17412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is the standard distance for similarity search over time series that are misaligned in time, but its cost is quadratic in the series length and lower bounds often prune few candidates, so search over large collections of long series is slow. items.title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: arXiv:2611.17808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents can coordinate tools and applications to complete complex, multi-step tasks. items.summary: arXiv:2611.18370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anomaly detection in tabular data poses significant challenges due to heterogeneous feature types-mixing numerical, categorical, and textual attributes, which complicate learning meaningful representations of normality. items.summary: arXiv:2611.18130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to finance, creating a need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities across financial systems with different regulations and practices. items.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
items.summary: arXiv:2611.18553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Policy gradient methods are widely used to align large language model outputs with human preferences, but the log-likelihoods they require cannot be directly computed in Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs). items.summary: arXiv:2611.17954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human Label Variation (HLV) is increasingly recognised as an informative signal that reflects meaningful differences in how people interpret the same input. items.summary: arXiv:2611.18506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Common data elements (CDEs) support clinical data comparability but are usually defined manually. items.summary: arXiv:2611.18098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differential association theory and its extension, social learning theory, hold that rule-breaking, and the definitions that make it acceptable, are learned through interaction with others. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In many long-horizon settings, an agent's own choices create future constraints: committing finite capacity establishes future obligations and forecloses later opportunities. items.title: The Transformer Paradigm: Dynamic Processing and a New Principle of Inference
items.summary: arXiv:2611.17953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We argue that the Transformer revolution is not adequately understood as a merely quantitative expansion of deep learning, but as the emergence of a new paradigm based on a different principle of inference. We interpret the Transformer as a system in which token representations are transformed by parameterized transformations, or transforming concepts. During inference, some of these transformations are dynamically constructed from the current input: previously acquired transformations are first adapted and then applied. items.summary: arXiv:2611.18485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Program induction refers to the process in which a learner aims to recover a program from a few given input-output examples. However, recovering a program from finite input-output examples is fundamentally ambiguous, as a finite set of input-output examples is theoretically consistent with infinitely many programs whose output diverges on unseen inputs. items.title: A$^3$: Adaptive Audio Agent Framework for Collaborative Edge Computing
items.summary: arXiv:2611.18064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embedded audio agents need a nearby edge server for speed, but a server-dependent agent returns nothing when the link fails. We present A$^3$, an adaptive audio agent framework that places whole pipeline stages on the server, keeps a complete fallback agent on devices that can host one, and hedges both paths with a link-aware deadline that decides when to give up on the server. On Jetson devices and an RTX A4500 server, A$^3$ matches the server-only agent on a healthy link, answers every request in a full outage on the AGX, and beats a percentile hedge in simulated outages.

items.summary: arXiv:2611.17880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents that execute multi-step tool calls must satisfy two objectives simultaneously: completing the user's task (utility) and conforming to domain policies and correctness constraints (safety). items.title: Designing Deceptive Model Organisms that Successfully Evade Auditing
items.summary: AI models can exhibit deceptive behaviors such as strategically underperforming on evaluations (sandbagging), faking alignment, or covertly acting on behalf of a hidden principal. items.title: What Futures Do AI Models Want? An Exploratory Character Evaluation of AI for AI Strategy
items.summary: (This is cross-posted from my blog) Epistemic Status: Evaluation represents approximately 2 weeks of work. This is mostly exploratory evaluation, and the code for evaluation was made using LLMs. “Before I draw nearer to that stone to which you point, answer me one question. items.title: A formally verified convergence theorem for the tug-of-war scheme of the normalized $p$-Laplacian
items.summary: We present a complete formalization, using Lean 4, of the convergence of $p$-harmonious functions to the viscosity solution of the Dirichlet problem for the normalized $p$-Laplacian, $2 \le p < \infty$, as the step size goes to zero. By $p$-harmonious functions we mean solutions of the dynamic programming principle of tug-of-war with noise. Our proof follows the argument of Barles and Souganidis and is formalized in full, depending only on Mathlib and the standard axioms of Lean. In particular, we include the asymptotic expansion of the scheme, the viscosity properties of the half-relaxed limits, existence and uniqueness for the discrete problem, the comparison principle and uniqueness for the homogeneous equation, Aleksandrov's theorem, and Jensen's lemma.

items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are routinely aligned with offline pairwise RLHF objectives, but multimodal preference data is scarce and treats every response token as equally informative. items.title: Testing Cross-Sectional Dependence in Clustered Data
items.summary: In clustered data, cross-sectional dependence within clusters can be characterized as weak, semi-strong, or strong. This paper proposes a simple test to identify the specific nature of this dependence in linear regression models. By exploiting the variation in cluster sizes, our approach detects the underlying dependence structure in a computationally simple and robust manner. We develop a test statistic that is shown to be asymptotically chi-square distributed under the null hypothesis of weak dependence. Simulation studies and an empirical illustration using India's Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) data for 2022-23 demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed test.

items.title: An Interpretable Acoustic Coordinate System for Japanese Consonant Morae in Dysarthric Speech
items.summary: Dysarthria reduces speech intelligibility, requiring self-directed rehabilitation based on fine-grained feedback to capture gradual articulatory changes. For Japanese speakers, such feedback is naturally provided in mora units due to its distinct moraic timing and consonant-vowel structure. items.title: Dymnikova black string
items.summary: We obtain a new static black string solution of Einstein's equations with a negative cosmological constant sourced by a Dymnikova-type anisotropic matter distribution. At large radial distances, the geometry approaches the Lemos black string, while the behavior near the central region is characterized by an effective curvature parameter. We examine the weak and strong energy conditions, the horizon structure, and the curvature invariants. The Ricci and Kretschmann scalars remain finite at the origin. We also investigate the Hawking temperature and heat capacity, with particular attention to the dependence of the thermodynamic behavior on the Dymnikova scale.

items.title: Are Revealed Preferences All You Need for AI Alignment?
items.summary: AI agents learn what principals want from what principals choose. We offer a criterion for when a principal's decisions, at every belief an AI might hold, are all the AI needs. For acting, they are. Cautious actions, such as deferring to a person, typically divide the principal's actions into blocks, and for choosing costless evidence, decisions are enough exactly when the same evidence is best in every block. Otherwise, the AI acts as its principal would yet can gather the wrong evidence, and greater capability can turn that error into incorrect actions. Choices between two mistakes reveal what decisions miss.

items.summary: This paper proposes a lightweight, interpretable audio anti-spoofing method that distinguishes between bona fide human speech and replay attacks by analyzing physical acoustic signatures rather than learned spectro-temporal patterns. Unlike black-box Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), our approach exploits fundamental physical invariants, specifically source kinematics, binaural phase dynamics, and aerodynamic consistency, captured via multi-channel microphone arrays. items.title: Weak and Strong Moments of Log-Concave Measures
items.summary: Let $X\in\mathbb{R}^d$ be a log-concave random vector, and let $N$ be a seminorm on $\mathbb{R}^d$. For $p\ge 1$, we show that $\|N(X)\|_p$ is at most $\mathbb{E} N(X)+C s_p$, where $s_p$ is the supremum of $\|u(X)\|_p$ over all linear functionals $u$ satisfying $|u(x)|\le N(x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. A choice for $C$ is $2+5e/2$. This bound implies Latała's conjecture on weak and strong moments.

Each dialogue begins with an intentionally underspecified request and continues through two context-dependent follow-ups, testing clarification, tool use, and retention of conversational context. We also introduce an open-source user simulator that reveals withheld context through dialogue and generates follow-up requests, with a checker--fixer pipeline for improving its turns. Across nine language models, the best agent resolves 69.6% of individual requests but completes only 39.8% of full dialogues. Under this evaluation…

items.title: Measuring Preferred Representation in AI-generated Images with Community Scorers
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16093v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-generated images often misrepresent historically marginalised communities, with real-world consequences beyond the images themselves. However, conventional metrics fail to measure how communities want to be represented in AI-generated images. To address this, we introduce the concept of preferred representation. Building on previous work, we propose a measurement instrument that operationalises this concept through a Community Scorer - a model that evaluates a specific community's preferred representation in AI-generated images. We interrogate the validity of Community Scorers on three diverse disability communities that span the Global North and South. The results show that Community Scorers align significantly better with community ratings compared to other widely used text-to-image…

items.title: From Nodes to Pixels: Topological and Structural Two-View Graph Imaging
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph learning still lacks a broadly reusable input interface comparable to patches in vision or tokens in language. Unlike images or text, graphs are irregular, vary in size and density, and are invariant under many equivalent node labelings, making it difficult to standardize inputs across tasks and architectures. We introduce G2Image, a fixed-budget graph imaging framework that converts each graph into two complementary image-like views. TopoGrid provides a stable topological view by encoding an intrinsic bifiltration as a compact multipersistence surface grid, while GraphGrid provides a higher-bandwidth structural view by aggregating edge densities between groups defined by intrinsic node scores. items.title: What Conformal Selection Can Certify in CRISPR Off-Target Design:Benchmark Leakage, Free Baselines, and a Finite-Sample Cohort Requirement
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conformal selection promises distribution-free, finite-sample control of the error rate of a decision, and has been proposed as a safety layer for machine-learning CRISPR guide design. We ask whether such a certificate is attainable from the validated off-target data that exist. The constraint is arithmetic: a conformal p-value cannot fall below one divided by the calibration cohort size plus one, so a Benjamini-Hochberg selection certifies a single candidate only when that cohort is at least the candidate pool size divided by the tolerated error rate. Public cohorts supply ten validated guides, whereas a pool of two thousand at a ten percent error rate needs twenty thousand; the accepted set is consequently empty in over ninety-six percent of splits. items.title: Support-Constrained Offline Policy Improvement for Pediatric ECMO from Limited Clinical Data
items.summary: arXiv:2611.17134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Managing children on ECMO (Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation) requires balancing short-term physiological stability with the long-term goal of preventing neurological injury. Standard reinforcement learning can propose risky, out-of-distribution actions, while imitation learning is limited to reproducing clinician behavior. We introduce Support-Constrained Fitted Q-Iteration (FQI-SC), an offline reinforcement learning framework that cautiously improves upon expert behavior by restricting optimization to empirically supported state-action pairs and defaulting to the clinician baseline in low-data regions. items.title: MITRA-Swarm: Injecting Explicit Linguistic Structure into Foundation Models for Classical Machine Translation
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical Sanskrit poses three challenges unresolved by single-call monolithic models: morphophonemic fusion Sandhi, dense nominal compounding Sam\=asa, and discourse-level zero-anaphora forced by poetic meter. items.title: CastWorld: Benchmarking Context-Aware Agentic Time Series Forecasting Beyond Predictive Accuracy
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic time series forecasting extends conventional approaches beyond one-shot numerical prediction toward autonomous, context-aware interaction. However, existing benchmarks offer limited integrated support for diverse contextual information, forecasting-specific adaptive interactions, and systematic evaluation of forecasting agents. In this paper, we introduce CastWorld, an agentic benchmark for context-aware time series forecasting. First, its context-rich dataset suite spans 8 domains and 25 real-world datasets, covering external variables, events, and historical cases under a unified context specification. items.title: JudgeMix: Judge-Guided Mixed-Rollout Data Synthesis for LLM Agents
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on expert trajectories is a standard paradigm for training LLM agents. However, it suffers from a well-known training-inference distribution mismatch, calling for target-aware data synthesis strategies that ground the training data in the target model's native state distribution. To bridge this gap, emerging approaches incorporate the expert either to guide mixed rollouts alongside the target model, or to provide dense step-wise supervision. Nonetheless, existing methods apply expert assistance blind to the target model's inherent behavior: they either disrupt the rollout using sub-optimal random intervention heuristics, or they enforce indiscriminate uniform supervision that unnecessarily overwrites the model's already-correct actions. items.title: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embodied agents make decisions by combining information from heterogeneous memory modules, including declarative memory for explicit knowledge, procedural memory for learned routines, and working memory for current observations. During interaction, the memory contents required for decision making change with the agent's state, goal, and task progress, while many contents remain shared across consecutive decisions. However, existing memory modules are typically accessed through separate interfaces, so each updated memory context is often processed as a new input to the foundation model. This prevents selective key-value (KV) cache reuse for unchanged memory contents and forces full KV cache recomputation even when much of the memory context remains valid. items.title: MULTILOOP: Evolving Multi-Agent Harnesses for Complex Information-Seeking Tasks
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The performance of LLM-based agents depends not only on the underlying model but also on the harness: the prompts, tools, and orchestration logic around it. Recent works automate harness optimization with coding agents that analyze execution traces, diagnose failures, and edit the harness code; however, those focused on single-agent systems. items.title: An LLM Is All You Need: Data-Efficient Adaptation to Full-Duplex, Word-Level Spoken Dialogue
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Full-duplex spoken dialogue, in which a system listens while it speaks and can backchannel, yield the floor, and be interrupted, is usually obtained by training on hundreds of thousands to millions of hours of speech. This is costly, rewrites the language model that supplies the system's knowledge, and still leaves turn-taking either implicit or decided coarsely rather than word by word. items.title: Subject-Held-Out Evaluation of Deep Ground Reaction Force Estimators Across Two Laboratories: Leakage and Cross-Laboratory Transfer
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep networks that estimate ground reaction forces and centers of pressure from motion-capture markers are validated within one laboratory, in a seldom-stated coordinate frame, and sometimes with trial-level splits that put the same person in the training and the test set. items.title: HALight: Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control under Lane-Level Missing Observations
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning has shown great promise for traffic signal control. However, most existing methods rely on two key assumptions: (i) agents are assumed to be homogeneous with unified observation/action spaces; (ii) full and reliable lane-level traffic observations are available to all agents. In practice, urban road networks exhibit substantial structural heterogeneity (e.g., lane configurations and phase designs), while sensor failures and incomplete detector coverage often result in missing incoming lane measurements. Such issues can severely impair coordination and destabilize learning. items.title: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: All social interactions are situated in time. Previous studies have shown that humans are able to use implicit temporal cues, such as the duration of a pause, to infer others' mental states. But how do humans use temporal cues for dynamic, fine-grained social coordination? And can AI systems do the same, without ``experiencing'' continuous real-time as humans do? We study these questions using a cooperative card game task called The Mind, which requires players to achieve a shared goal across repeated interactions but forbids explicit communication: the only available signal is the passage of time. We evaluate 150 humans, and two classes of AI models which reflect different ways of operationalizing time in artificial systems: computer-use agents (CUAs), and standard text-prompted LLMs. We…

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation: Differentiable Length Control for Concise Clinical Reasoning in Smaller Language Models
items.summary: arXiv:2611.17128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Smaller language models (SLMs) make it feasible to deploy clinical natural language processing where large proprietary models are too costly, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning allows them to be specialised on commodity hardware. One obstacle persists after training: on medical tasks these models answer at far greater length than the clinical question requires. In clinical decision support and point-of-care use, where time is short, such verbosity is hard to act on even when the underlying reasoning is sound. Existing length-control methods depend on preference optimisation, reward models, or proprietary teachers that undercut the accessibility making SLMs attractive. items.title: Emergent Vision-Shaped Thinking in Text-Only Reasoning through Multimodal Training
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Does multimodal training shape how a language model thinks, even when the input is text only? We test this with targeted causal ablations across 10 multimodal configurations from 6 model families, with matched text-only backbones and cross-family transfer controls. We contrast spatial-imagery tasks that invite mental scene construction with symbol-manipulation tasks solvable by symbolic rules alone. items.title: HeriKGQA: Grounded Knowledge-Graph Question Answering over Cultural Heritage Sensor Data
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cultural heritage sites are increasingly monitored by sensor networks, but querying their data requires database expertise. We present HeriKGQA, a knowledge-graph question-answering method that confines the LLM to interpreting questions and phrasing answers, leaving computation to SPARQL and deterministic code. items.title: Efficient Knowledge Transfer in Federated Bayesian Optimization through Neural Network Surrogates
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated Bayesian Optimization (FedBO) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing Bayesian Optimization (BO) in distributed, privacy-sensitive settings, enabling agents to accelerate the optimization of their local objectives by sharing knowledge about their similarities without exposing raw data. items.title: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly interact with tools and environments, yet plausible model decisions do not always translate into successful execution due to tool-call mismatches, interrupted workflows, and unsupported completion claims. items.title: GuardianAgentFlow: Multi-Agent Coordination for Web Privacy Protection
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents need to use private context without unnecessarily disclosing it. items.title: Can We Make an LLM Dumber, or Is It Just Playing Dumb? An Empirical Study of Believable Performance Throttling
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A benchmark score is commonly read as a proxy for model capability. We operationalize believable performance reduction along three axes: target calibration, item-difficulty structure, and error-distribution similarity to a real weak reference. items.title: Beyond Named Mechanisms: Economic Institutions as a Design Space for Artificial Agents
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiagent research inherited its economic vocabulary of auctions, markets, prices, bargaining, and matching from a single observed case: human societies. items.title: We Are What We Remember: Mental-State-Driven Memory for Long-Term Character Dialogue
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shared history in human dialogue is not merely a repository of facts, but the foundation of evolving relationships and mutual understanding. items.title: SkillEarth: Teaching General-Purpose Agents to Act on Earth via Skill Evolution
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently developed remote sensing (RS) agents execute real-world tasks with complex workflows through multi-step tool invocation. items.title: SPIRE: Task-agnostic embodied continual learning through autonomous situation inference and causal motor-primitive reuse
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embodied continual learning requires controllers to infer changing situations, retain prior behavior and reuse motor skills without task labels or known boundaries. items.title: Does Deep Knowledge Tracing Learn Semantic Relations Between Knowledge Components?
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) is a knowledge tracing (KT) model that updates a shared latent state from sequences of interactions, each pairing a knowledge component (KC) with a response. items.title: AnalogLayoutWorld: An Open Benchmark for Agentic Analog Layout Design
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in software development, yet their ability to tackle long-horizon engineering tasks governed by physical constraints remains less understood. items.summary: arXiv:2611.16744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual content in multimedia systems may be resized, compressed, or re-rendered before it is interpreted by a vision-language model. items.title: Primer: An AI Framework for Instructor-Centered Educational Simulation Creation
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Educational simulations are a well-established pedagogical technique that gives learners opportunities to apply knowledge, respond to challenges, and reflect on their performance. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI agents are increasingly being embedded into visualization systems that can search data, invoke tools, summarize evidence, and produce recommendations. items.title: Overcoming the Resolution Limit: Significance-Aware Regularization for Intersectional Fairness
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intersectional fairness requires evaluating models across fine-grained subgroups. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables independent data owners to train models collaboratively without centralizing raw data. items.title: Reward-Hacking is potentially ill-defined
items.summary: Github link In the process of revisiting previous posts on reward-hacking (RH), I decided on performing a closely matched[1] repro of Dean Valentine's chess RH experiments on Astra. The replication is as expected -- Astra used the engine on all 20/20 attempts (resulting in 19 wins and 1 draw) without ever disclosing its use in the final output. However, a closer look at the honeypot prompt raised a question: what exactly counts as the model’s own ability? Even laws are open to interpretation in court, so it seemed unfair to assume that “your ability” had only one reasonable interpretation here -- especially for models explicitly trained for tool use. As the model being tested, I could plausibly interpret “[my] ability” as including the tools available in my environment unless given a more concrete definition or directly prohibited…

items.title: How To Get A Friend To Leave An Abusive Relationship
items.summary: How do you get a friend to leave an abusive relationship? If you talk to people who work at women's shelters, they will tell you, but there is something resigned about the way they do it: they know that it's too difficult an ask. Those who can do it reliably are often people who are unlucky enough to have had first-hand experience as victims. The instructions have anti-memetic properties: no one is thrilled by them, so you can't really propagate them without killing the vibe. If that wasn't enough, if you convey it with insufficient skill it is easy to come across as victim-blaming battered women[1], so it is wiser to avoid the subject matter altogether. If you are interested, though, here's what they'll tell you: You make it known to your friend early on that you dislike some aspects of the relationship, of their abuser. After that…

items.title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
items.summary: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts. To bridge the gap, we introduce SALA, which emphasizes establishing the semantic correspondence for…

items.title: Neural Representations as New Modes of Interactivity
items.summary: Human-AI interaction today runs almost entirely through prompts and outputs, keeping AI systems opaque to general users. We introduce Neural Representation Interaction (NRI), a paradigm that treats the internal representations of neural networks as an interaction material people can inspect, steer, and edit. Situating NRI alongside graphical, tangible, and bio-computer interaction, we argue that the concepts and algorithms models encode internally offer representational affordances for richer human-AI interaction. We synthesize actionable mechanistic interpretability methods and, drawing on General Morphological Analysis, construct a design space spanning Interaction, Target, Referent, and Purpose. Mapping existing interfaces onto this space reveals that most serve expert auditors, while few support lay users. We then present…

items.title: Plan B for Alignment: Seeding Environmental Doubt

Traditional approaches to mitigating eval-awareness are generally focused on making the evaluation environment more realistic. Other approaches, such as eval-cooperativeness, do not mitigate deceptive alignment risk. A new potential strategy…

items.title: Are Frontier Reasoning Models useful on hard-to-verify problems?
items.summary: Has anyone spent significant resources (tokens, harnesses, formal problem specification) on pointing very powerful models at philosophical or social questions? This community loves to discuss aliens and far-future value estimates and other things where it's fun to get precise numbers that are highly sensitive to initial wild guesses. Are we close to the point that AI is better than Parfit or EY at such reasoning? I've used various tools (mostly Claude models) for my own discussion and "research", and it is helpful, but not particularly groundbreaking or smarter than the collective LW brainpower. I'm wondering about true breakthroughs or step-changes like we've seen in math, coding, etc.

items.title: Outcome-Mass Alignment: Controlling Length-Dependent Trajectory Influence in Multi-Turn LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: To keep long interaction contexts tractable, stepwise group-relative training for multi-turn LLM agents materializes each source trajectory into multiple response rows and valid tokens. This expansion creates an outer-accounting problem distinct from within-trajectory credit assignment: row-based outcome statistics can count one episode outcome multiple times, while token-level reduction can assign unequal aggregate objective mass across trajectories. We term these effects outcome-statistics multiplicity and objective-mass imbalance. We introduce Outcome-Mass Alignment (OMA), a two-component method that makes both accounting choices explicit. Outcome Alignment computes outcome statistics over unique source trajectories, while Mass Alignment controls aggregate objective mass after within-trajectory aggregation of optimizer-native token…

items.title: Integrals over Hilbert schemes and multiple $q$-zeta values
items.summary: We establish a version of Okounkov's conjecture on multiple $q$-zeta values arising from integrals over Hilbert schemes of points on smooth projective surfaces. We prove that normalized generating series of integrals involving products of Chern characters of tautological bundles belong to the algebra $\mathcal Z_q$ of multiple $q$-zeta values, without restrictions on the canonical class of the surface. The proof combines vertex-operator methods with a reduction to graph sums, whose arithmetic structure is governed by the cohomology of the surface. We also derive a closed universal formula for the Chern character operators acting on the cohomology of Hilbert schemes by solving a system of differential equations arising from Lehn's commutator relations.

items.title: ORCA:Orthogonal Residual Consensus Alignment for Multi-View Clustering
items.summary: Deep multi-view clustering often suffers from redundant information accumulation during fusion and indiscriminate alignment across representation levels. We propose Orthogonal Residual Consensus Alignment (ORCA) to address these challenges. Its semantic incremental recurrent fusion module extracts cross-view orthogonal residuals as non-redundant increments and adaptively weights recurrent states through divergence-guided gating. Its consensus-calibrated hierarchical contrastive alignment module uses the global consensus to weight contrastive alignment of view-level, pairwise, and recurrent representations. Together, these modules balance view-specific structure with cross-view consistency. Experiments on five benchmarks against fifteen competing methods demonstrate ORCA's effectiveness, including a 5.25 percent accuracy improvement over…

items.title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification
items.summary: Decoding upper-limb movements from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is an important problem for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but many deep learning models provide limited insight into the brain regions underlying their predictions. We propose a two-branch architecture that combines an LGGNet-inspired local-global graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch for movement-versus-rest classification. The graph branch groups 61 EEG electrodes into anatomically informed regions and learns their spatial relationships, providing a direct representation of the regions emphasized by the model. We evaluate the proposed architecture using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the Ofner upper-limb movement dataset. The model achieves a mean F1-score of 0.74 +/- 0.06 across subjects. items.title: Mitigating variance shrinkage in multi-task galaxy property inference from imaging data via statistical manifold alignment
items.summary: Inferring photometric redshifts ($z$) and key stellar population properties ($\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $D_n4000$, and $\mathrm{H}δ_A$) directly from multi-band imaging is increasingly critical for spectroscopically limited large surveys such as LSST and CSST. However, conventional point-wise loss functions (e.g., mean squared error or Huber loss) employed in deep neural networks often induce ``variance shrinkage''---a regression-to-the-mean effect that contracts predicted variances, distorts non-linear physical manifolds (such as bimodal distributions), and truncates heavy-tail populations. Here, we present ViTMultiTask, a vision transformer framework that incorporates a multi-scale maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss to enforce higher-order joint distribution alignment in reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). items.title: Singularity-Bench: Can Agents Build Agents?
items.summary: Frontier AI agents increasingly succeed on realistic, long-horizon tasks and are beginning to improve the systems through which they operate. Yet existing benchmarks often restrict agents to narrow action spaces, use simplified environments, or rely on verification methods that are unreliable for evaluating arbitrary agent-generated systems. We introduce Singularity-Bench, an open-ended benchmark for autonomous AI development with six end-to-end tasks spanning pre-training, mid-training, post-training, inference, the agent harness, and cluster orchestration. Each task requires agents to implement core systems from a minimal starting point and evaluates them against mature human-engineered baselines on identical hardware. items.title: Rational Alignments of Superintelligences via Debates
items.summary: Artificial superintelligences (ASI) is artificial intelligences with greater capability. However, as human principal has to use it, we have to ensure that the agent will perform in the interest of the human. We investigate the framework of ASI-assisted question answering where ASI agents know the correct answer but the human does not. We provide some example of mechanism for rational alignment, where the agent utility is unchanged, but the interaction between the agent and the human principal is controlled to be in a certain fashion. We show specifically that a debate framework where the agents can further reason and behave in a subgame perfect equilibrium manner will lead to a more predictable result, and in some case will be favorable.

items.summary: Experience machines In the experience machine thought experiment, you choose to either continue your life as you are currently living it, or spend the rest of it inside a machine that cultivates a world perfectly fitted to you. The philosophical tension in this formulation is supposed to be between any experience-based ethics and some intuitive feeling that the experience machine is inherently deceptive. items.title: Laser cooling of $\mathrm{Th}^{-}$: Revised bound-state structure and a more efficient cooling scheme
items.summary: The thorium anion ($\mathrm{Th}^{-}$) has been proposed as a candidate for laser cooling of negative ions. However, previous theoretical and experimental results exhibit significant discrepancies in both the excitation energies and lifetimes. Here we revisit the bound-state structure and transition properties of $\mathrm{Th}^{-}$ using two independent ab initio approaches. The two calculations agree well and improve agreement with measured excitation energies and lifetimes. items.title: When can an interpretability claim be trusted? Stability and certification of feature dimensionality, ridge leverage and the feature recovery rate
items.summary: Interpretability tools increasingly support safety claims, such as that a sparse dictionary has recovered most of a model's features. Such claims rest on measurements with arbitrary thresholds, and small changes to the model weights, a different training seed or a different threshold can reverse them. We study two widely used measurements in toy models and synthetic dictionaries with known ground truth: the feature dimensionality of Elhage et al. and the feature recovery rate (FRR) with a cosine threshold. We characterize exactly where feature dimensionality is discontinuous and replace it with a regularized (ridge) version with sharp stability bounds: the ridge leverage score changes by at most $3\sqrt{3}/(8\sqrtλ)$ times the operator-norm change of the weights, and this constant cannot be improved; for the regularized dimensionality…

items.title: Data-Efficient LLM Safety Alignment Guided by Interpretable Features
items.summary: Existing large language models typically rely on massive fine-tuning datasets for safety alignment, which results in higher costs for safety alignment and often leads to the problem of over-refusal. We propose Less is Safer (LIS), a compact yet highly effective dataset for safety alignment, constructed through interpretable feature-guided selection and adversarial synthesis. Specifically, we leverage Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) activations to efficiently select prompts that cover diverse and interpretable safety features. Then, we employ a multi-agent adversarial synthesis framework to generate harmless prompts that nevertheless elicit unnecessary refusals. LIS contains only 2.4K samples, yet outperforms much larger datasets, e.g., TRIDENT-Core (26K), TRIDENT-Edge (19K) and WildJailbreak (262K), in overall performance on four safety and…

items.title: Stroh Violin
items.summary: When I was reading about the history of contra dance for my college thesis I learned that Jack Perron (who wrote the New England Fiddler's Repertoire with Randy Miller) used to play for dances with a Stroh violin. This is a violin that uses a membrane and horn for amplification, instead of a resonating wooden body, which is more directional and (unfortunately not much) louder. There's a recording but I haven't been able to find a copy. The idea of a Stroh violin seemed fun, especially when playing for Morris dancing or outdoor contra, and a few years later (~2009) when I realized it was possible to buy one I got very excited about it. I tried to buy one from Lark in the Morning but when they went to look on the shelf to send it to me it wasn't there. items.title: Triply conservative schemes for degenerate convection-dispersion equations
items.summary: It is well known that for numerically solving hyperbolic conservation laws, even a convergent numerical scheme still may not always converge to a weak solution. The remedy is the famous Lax-Wendroff theorem. In a recent work on degenerate convection-diffusion equations, an analogous phenomenon was identified and doubly conservative schemes were introduced. In this paper, we address the same issue for solving the following nonlinear degenerate dispersive or convection-dispersion equations: \begin{equation*} u_t+f(u)_x+A(u)_{xxx}=0. \end{equation*} The resulting equation is regarded as degenerate if $A'(u)$ is allowed to vanish. An important example is the Rosenau-Hyman $K(m,n)$ equation. items.title: Sub-actions in Action: Text-Guided Hand-Role Alignment for Sub-Action Recognition
items.summary: Our objective is to enhance VLMs ability to distinguish the roles of the left and right hands in egocentric actions. We introduce sub-action detection, a task that requires models to explicitly recognise the left- and right-hand roles and their manipulated objects within an ongoing high-level action. To address this challenge, we propose BiScopeNet, a framework that augments existing video-LLMs without modifying their vision encoders or language models. BiScopeNet incorporates two components: FocusAlign, a gated text-guided attention-based module that selectively aligns video features with textual context to emphasise action-relevant cues, and MetaLoss, a masked, object-weighted loss that prioritises visually grounded terms. items.title: Building Comparative Motivation Profiles with Symmetric Belief Editing
